steps.title: Record isolate information
steps.instruction: Document the isolate number(s) and the lyophilized date(s) for each vial in a laboratory notebook or electronic record.

steps.title: Disinfect vial and remove stopper
steps.instruction: Wipe the aluminum cap and the outside of the vial with isopropyl alcohol. Using sturdy forceps, aseptically remove the aluminum cover and rubber stopper. Wipe the outside of the rubber stopper and the vial neck with isopropyl alcohol before fully removing the stopper.

steps.title: Resuspend lyophilized cells
steps.instruction: Add 1 ml of sterile reagent‑grade water (or 1 ml sterile phosphate‑buffered saline if specified) to the vial. Allow the suspension to stand for a few minutes and/or mix gently until a uniform suspension is achieved.

substeps.instruction: a) Transfer 10 µl of the suspension onto a blood agar plate (BAP). Streak as a spot, plate in duplicate, and incubate at 37 °C overnight in aerobic conditions.

b) Transfer 100 µl of the suspension onto each of two non‑selective BHI‑RBC (BHIRB) plates. Plate in duplicate. Incubate one plate microaerobically at 42 °C for 48 h and the second plate microaerobically at 37 °C for 48 h.

steps.title: Inoculate broth for overnight culture
steps.instruction: Add the remaining suspension (approximately 0.99 ml) to 5 ml of Brain‑Heart Infusion (BHI) broth. Incubate the broth overnight at 37 °C in aerobic conditions.

steps.title: Check plates and subculture colonies
steps.instruction: On Day 2 (and Day 3 if needed), examine the plates from step 4:

substeps.instruction: For BAPs: if growth appears pure, pick an isolated colony and streak onto a fresh BAP. Incubate the new plate at 37 °C overnight aerobic.

For BHIRB plates: check both plates for purity, pick two isolated colonies, and streak each colony onto two fresh BHIRB plates (four plates total). Incubate one set microaerobically at 42 °C and the other set microaerobically at 37 °C for 48 h.

steps.title: Optional rescue plating if no growth
steps.instruction: If no bacterial growth is observed on the plates from step 4, take a sterile loop from the BHI overnight culture (step 5), streak onto a fresh BAP (or BHIRB plate as appropriate), and incubate at 37 °C overnight aerobic (or the temperature specified for the chosen plate type). Re‑check the plate the next day and continue as in step 6.

steps.title: Prepare sequencing sample sheet
steps.instruction: Complete the sequencing sample sheet (Table 1) with the exact strain identifiers (Sample_ID and Sample_Name) as printed on the lyophilized vial; do not modify these IDs. Fill the Project field with your lab name (e.g., USFDA_HFP_2026_Proficiency_Testing_Exercise). The Description field is optional and may contain organism names.

steps.title: Perform DNA extraction
steps.instruction: Extract genomic DNA from the overnight culture (or from the sub‑cultured plate) using your laboratory’s standard protocol, e.g., the Qiagen DNeasy Blood & Tissue Kit, following the GenomeTrakr and/or PulseNet SOPs.

steps.title: Quantify extracted DNA
steps.instruction: Measure DNA concentration using the laboratory‑approved method, such as the Qubit fluorometer, according to the GenomeTrakr/PulseNet SOPs.

steps.title: Prepare sequencing libraries
steps.instruction: Construct sequencing libraries following the Illumina DNA Prep (M) Tagmentation Library Preparation protocol (or your routine library‑prep SOP). Ensure the total genome loading meets the cartridge requirements and avoid >100× coverage. Include control reference strains if the number of isolates is insufficient to fill the run.

steps.title: Load and run sequencing
steps.instruction: Load the prepared libraries onto the Illumina MiSeq, NextSeq 1000/2000, or equivalent instrument using the normal routine‑run loading procedure described in the GenomeTrakr/PulseNet SOPs. Follow the instrument’s standard run parameters (e.g., chemistry, number of cycles, flow‑cell ID).

steps.title: Quality control sequencing data
steps.instruction: Perform quality control of the raw sequencing data using your laboratory’s normal workflow (e.g., GalaxyTrakr MicroRunQC workflow by Maria Balkey) as described in the GenomeTrakr and/or PulseNet SOPs.

steps.title: Transfer sequencing data
steps.instruction: After QC, transfer the acceptable data sets to the GenomeTrakr repository via BaseSpace, a shared network drive, or a BOX folder, following GenomeTrakr guidelines.

steps.instruction: If you prefer to share the project without sharing a specific run:

steps.title: Transfer files to FDA storage
steps.instruction: For laboratories within the FDA network, copy the complete sequencing run folder to the designated Isilon storage drive as required by internal policies.

steps.title: Notify GenomeTrakr of completion
steps.instruction: Email genometrakr@fda.hhs.gov with the subject line “2026 WGS Proficiency Testing_YourLabName”. Attach the completed sequencing sample sheet and include the following items in the body:

substeps.instruction: k. SOP Protocol (select PulseNet SOP or GenomeTrakr SOP)
